html:
Persian carpets are hand-knotted wool and silk carpets made in Iran, its most famous craft. Weaving is very old there, but the art reached its height in the royal workshops of the Safavid shahs in the 1500s and 1600s.

Under the Safavids, court painters drew the designs, of gardens, medallions, flowers and hunts, and workshops in Tabriz, Kashan and Isfahan wove them. The Ardabil Carpet, finished in 1539 or 1540 and now in London, is one of the most famous. Nomads and villages kept their own bold patterns.

In the 1800s European demand made carpets a major export, and they still are, though machine-made rugs and sanctions have hurt the trade. Weaving in Fars and Kashan was listed by UNESCO in 2010. See also Abbas the Great and Persia.
